To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Ca complexing agents EDTA and EGTA abolish ACTH stimulation of adrenal adenyl cyclase and epinephrine activation of fat cell ghosts, and that added Ca restores the hormone sensitivity of these enzymes.
Ca is required for ACTH stimulation and that Ca can regulate 3’,5’-AMP formation both by itself and in combination with other agents.

1) Ca ion is required for ACTH stimulation and epinephrine inhibition of the activity of adenyl cyclases in mitochondrial and microsome fractions from bovine adrenocortical tissue and in ghosts from fat cells; 2) the Ca requirement is not due to a direct action of Ca on cyclase activity, but to a requirement for a Ca ion dependent process which is essential for cyclase activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of calcium ion in hormone stimulation of adenylate cyclase activity.
the mechanism by which hormones act to stimulate the formation of cyclic AMP.
the role of Ca ion in the regulation of adenyl cyclases in various cell types.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ca is a regulatory agent in the adenyl cyclase system and that it may be a necessary cofactor for hormone stimulation of adenylate cyclase.
the hormone action is mediated via the formation of 3′, 5′-AMP and that this formation is dependent on the presence of Ca.
the hormone sensitive adenyl cyclase system is a complex one, and that the role of Ca is not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adenyl cyclase system is a Ca dependent system and that the hormone effect is to increase the sensitivity of the system to Ca.
the Ca ion is a necessary cofactor for the hormone action of ACTH and glucagon, but is inhibitory for the action of epinephrines.
Ca ion is a necessary cofactor for the action of ACTH and that Ca ion can also inhibit the activity of adenyl cyclases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calcium ion is a very important factor in the regulation of the enzyme activity of the adenylyl cyclase.
Ca is required for hormone stimulation of adenyl cylase.
Ca ion may be an intracellular mediator of hormone action, perhaps acting as a link between the hormone receptor and adenyl cyclase.
